Unlike the 2015 JCPOA—where Democratic cohesion largely protected President Obama's veto—a 123 Agreement with Saudi Arabia creates a unique cross-ideological coalition: progressive Democrats opposing the kingdom's human rights record and nuclear proliferation risks, joined by hawkish Republicans deeply skeptical of any pathway allowing Riyadh to enrich uranium or draw closer to a Chinese or Russian nuclear alternative. This convergence of nuclear proliferation fears and deep distrust of Saudi security guarantees makes the political alignment closer to the 2019 bipartisan veto-override attempts on Middle Eastern policy, but with higher legislative stakes that increase the probability of both chambers successfully clearing a joint resolution of disapproval.
